title: terraform: reorganize private GPU node pools, IAM roles, networking and state layout
author: Ava Khan
description:
Motivation: Private deployments have grown organic additions to Terraform modules for GPU node pools, IAM, and networking. This made state layout brittle for upgrades (customers running upgrades hit name collisions and manual state surgery). This PR reorganizes the private deployment Terraform modules to a clearer hierarchy, introduces a deterministic state layout migration path, and adds a GPU node-pool module with opinionated defaults (burst autoscaling, preemptible handling) suitable for Private deployments.

Changes included (high level):
- modules/private/gpu_node_pool: new dedicated module with main.tf, variables.tf, outputs.tf, and examples. The module encapsulates GKE/AKS/EC2 nodepool concerns (taints/labels, GPU accelerator type, machine types, autoscaler settings).
- modules/private/iam: refactor to split role definitions (control-plane roles, node pool roles, SRE/monitoring roles) and add granular condition-based bindings required for restricted private environments.
- modules/private/networking: minor refactors to make subnetwork and route creation optional when using customer-provisioned networking.
- modules/private/state_layout: introduced canonical backend config and README describing workspace naming, state key prefixes, and migration steps.
- scripts/state_migration.sh: opinionated helper to copy/rename state objects between S3/GCS keys for in-place upgrades; idempotent and prints a dry-run summary.
- examples/private/gke: added a worked example showing how to wire the new modules together with a sample backend and variables.tf for test clusters.
- docs/upgrade/private-state-migration.md: user-facing upgrade notes including preflight checks and rollback steps.
- .github/workflows/terraform.yml: extended CI to run module unit checks, terraform validate/plan against examples, and a smoke apply in sandbox env ( gated by secrets ).

Migration plan:
1) Run preflight: terraform plan with new backend config in a sandbox workspace.
2) Run scripts/state_migration.sh --dry-run against current backend and verify mapping.
3) Run migration script with backups enabled (copies state objects with timestamp suffix).
4) Update backend config in customers' control plane to new key prefix and re-run terraform init && plan.

Backward compatibility: Modules accept legacy variable aliases (legacy_node_pool_* envs) and include deprecation warnings in Terraform outputs for one release cycle. The state migration script supports both legacy and new key layouts.

Testing: Added unit test files for GPU module (tests/gpu_node_pool_test.tf) validated in CI. Local testing included spinning up a small GKE sandbox cluster and running a full plan/apply for the example (dev infra). CI initially failed on variable naming lint in the IAM module (see review thread) and on missing secrets for the sandbox apply; both were resolved and full CI passed before merge.

Rollout: Staged rollout: internal sandbox -> partner lab -> customer upgrades. Coordination ticket created (ENG-4122) to schedule weekend migrations for existing Private customers.

Rollback: Documented in docs/upgrade/private-state-migration.md: revert to backup state object and terraform init with original backend key. The migration script writes a manifest to help revert.

Notes: No behavior change to hosted API. This is infra-only and gated behind terraform module versioning. Operators upgrading should follow the migration doc and run the included script.

release_notes: Refactored Terraform modules for Private deployments: new gpu_node_pool module, clearer IAM/networking module boundaries, and a documented state layout with migration tooling. Operators must follow docs/upgrade/private-state-migration.md when upgrading existing states.
